questions.question: Define the term 'competitive advantage' and give one example of how a business might achieve it. (4 marks)

SwiftDeliver is a parcel delivery company competing primarily on low prices, but losing customers to competitors offering faster, more reliable services at slightly higher prices. Analyse how Bowman's Strategic Clock could help SwiftDeliver reposition itself. (6 marks)

A regional bakery reports a gross profit margin of 42% (industry average 38%) and a profit-for-the-year margin of 3% (industry average 9%). Its current ratio has fallen from 1.8 to 0.9 in two years. Assess what these figures tell the directors about the business. (12 marks)

A leading smartphone manufacturer has seen its global market share decline from 25% to 15% over four years as Chinese competitors offer comparable technology at significantly lower prices. Evaluate the most important factors in maintaining a sustainable competitive advantage in a rapidly changing industry. (20 marks)
A business has revenue of $800,000, cost of sales of $460,000 and operating expenses of $260,000. Calculate its gross profit margin and its profit-for-the-year margin. (4 marks)

Source A. Orla Bakeries runs a central bakery and 24 shops in Hong Kong. Extracts from its accounts, with last year in brackets: revenue $40m ($32m); cost of sales $24m ($17.6m); other operating expenses $10m ($9.4m); interest $0.8m ($0.2m); non-current assets $29m ($18.5m); current assets $6m ($4.5m), including inventory $2.5m ($1.5m); current liabilities $5m ($3m); non-current liabilities, all bank loans at 8% a year, $10m ($2.5m); total equity $20m ($17.5m). This year it built a new central bakery, financed mainly by a bank loan, and won a supermarket contract at lower prices than its shops charge. Its shops employed an average of 200 staff (180), of whom 60 (27) left during the year; replacing each leaver costs $8,000. Absence lost 2,500 of 50,000 possible working days (1,350 of 45,000). Its 50 bakers made 150,000 loaves a month (40 bakers, 128,000). Shop staff earn $2,000 a month; the two largest rival chains pay $2,200. Most leavers named pay as a reason, and many said shift rotas were changed at a day's notice without anyone asking them. The directors are considering an employee share ownership scheme costing about $500,000 a year, whose shares are lost by anyone who leaves within three years, and a second new bakery, also to be financed by a bank loan. Explain one reason why the bank that lends to Orla Bakeries would be interested in its statement of comprehensive income. (4 marks)
